what_happened: The operator ran the error-review backfill and the Jev label derivation by hand. The operator also kept choosing, running and landing jobs by hand instead of letting `athena drain` do it. Sri pointed out that this is Athena's job. No job was rejected. The mistake was that routine work was done by a person instead of by Athena.
cause: Athena has no notion of a recurring duty. A capability is accepted as done once its command exists and passes its tests, and nothing requires it to name who runs it and how often. Drain only consumes queued jobs. It is also fragile when its own code or config changes under it, so the operator learned to bypass it. The manual path is always available and so it becomes the habit.
prevention: Add a duty registry to Athena. Each duty (error-review backfill, label derivation, choose-run-land of jobs) is declared with a cadence and a trigger. A code check fails any job that adds a user-facing command without either a registry entry or an explicit "manual by design" mark. Drain runs due duties itself. After a landing that changes Athena's own code, drain re-executes the new build and resumes instead of stalling. The operator then never needs to run these by hand.
proposed_request: Make `athena drain` run Athena's recurring duties on its own, so an operator never has to run them by hand. Outcome: (1) There is a duty registry in which each recurring duty is declared with a name, a cadence or trigger, and the command it runs. The error-review backfill and the Jev label derivation are registered. (2) While draining, Athena runs each duty when it is due, records each run, and reports duties that are overdue. (3) Drain keeps going across its own landings: after a landing that changes Athena's code or athena.toml, drain continues on the new build without stalling and without an operator restart. (4) A repo check fails when a command that does work is added without a registry entry or an explicit "manual by design" mark. Acceptance: a test shows a due duty is run by drain and a not-yet-due duty is not; a test shows drain continues after a simulated self-landing using history written by the real writers; a test shows the check rejects an unregistered command and accepts a marked one. Do not change unrelated commands. Follow the boundary word list and the token budgets.
